title: Level validity test
description: Since a new level is mostly data, add a vitest that runs over every LEVELS entry: every spawn edge/alley reaches a base on the flow field; no base overlaps a rock or ravine; waves reference only existing zombies; final wave has a boss; plants placeable somewhere. Catches typos in new levels.

title: Split config.ts by kind and per-level files
description: src/data/config.ts is 581 lines mixing types, plants, zombies, abilities, maps, themes, waves, sound. Split into data/plants.ts, zombies.ts, abilities.ts, themes.ts, sound.ts, and data/levels/neon.ts, levels/rust.ts (each owning map + theme + waves). Both levels share WAVES today; give each level its own so they can diverge. Keep a data/index.ts re-export so callers barely change.

title: Enforce sim layering with import rules
description: ADR 0002 says src/sim has no Babylon/render code, but nothing enforces it. Add ESLint no-restricted-imports (or dependency-cruiser): src/sim/** may import only src/sim and src/data; never @babylonjs/*, render/, ui/, models/. Wire into npm test / CI. Known violation today: src/data/config.ts imports ModelId from src/models — allowlist it until the looks/stats split bead removes it.

title: Level 3: Cyber Cemetery (futuristic graveyard)
description: New level: night graveyard. Neon-saber iron fence, rows of tombstones (rocks), big central hill with a creepy gazebo (rock), ghosts rising from graves, green slime, haunted houses + big moon in the distance. Zombies only from the north (back). Short ravine maze leads them to spaceship, then power plant, then greenhouse.

title: Guardian leap bobs up and down instead of jumping forward
description: The leap-and-slice gait bounced in place while the sim slid the Guardian along, which looked silly. Wanted: jump forward in an arc, slice on landing, stand up, repeat.
close_reason: Gait now plants, arcs forward (render-only stride offset that averages to the sim position), slices low in front on landing, holds, stands up. Attacking: hop-and-slash on the spot.

title: Golden replay tests
description: Record seed + command log, replay headless, compare a hash of final state. Catches unintended behavior changes the balance tests let through. Add a debug button to export the current game's log.

title: Serializable sim state and seed in URL
description: RNG is a mulberry32 closure, so state can't be saved; store the RNG state as a numeric field. Make Game state plain data (toJSON/fromJSON). main.ts seeds from Date.now(); accept ?seed= and show the seed in debug so any game is reproducible.

title: Split Game into systems
description: src/sim/game.ts is 825 lines. Keep Game as the state owner and step() orchestrator; move logic into spawning.ts, combat.ts, movement/*.ts, economy.ts, abilities.ts. Pure refactor; tests unchanged.

title: Player actions as command objects
description: Route place/sell/rotatePlant/startWave/useAbility through game.apply(cmd) with a typed Command union. Enables replay logs (bug -> exact repro test), build-phase undo, and a clean seam for saves or multiplayer.

title: Behavior tables for zombie movement, plant attacks, abilities
description: updateZombies in src/sim/game.ts branches def.giant -> zb.leader -> def.flying -> walker; each new zombie adds a branch and an optional ZombieDef field. Add movement: 'walker'|'flyer'|'giant'|'escort' (and plant attack kinds, ability kinds) with Record<Id, handler> tables in their own modules. A new zombie becomes a module + table entry, no game.ts edits. Balance tests must stay green.

title: Separate zombie looks from sim stats
description: ZombieDef mixes sim stats (hp, speed, armor) with looks (model, skin, hair, weapon, scale, art, color). Move looks to a render-side ZOMBIE_LOOKS: Record<ZombieId, …> (same for plant/structure art). Removes the data->models import and the layering-rule allowlist entry; art changes no longer touch balance data.

title: Add ESLint with typescript-eslint
description: strict is on; add typescript-eslint (recommended-type-checked) for floating promises, exhaustive switches, etc. Run in CI alongside tests. Can share setup with the import-rules bead.

title: Robustness & extensibility: architecture cleanup
description: Keep the 2D-sim / data-driven-level shape (ADR 0002, 0008) healthy as zombies, plants and levels grow. Children are filed in the recommended order: guard rails first (cheap, make later work safer), then sim behavior tables and commands (biggest extensibility win), then render/session seams.

title: Mid-battle weather

title: Buildings collapse when Giants stomp nearby
description: Rust Corridor buildings become individually collapsible; a Giant stomp or orbital strike near the street edge crumbles the nearest building: sinks and tilts, dust cloud, flying bricks, rubble left behind.

title: ADR: Art is generated in code, with drop-in hooks for Wesley's art
description:
Placeholder and scenery art is procedural: neon primitives, skins
painted by a generator script, and canvas-drawn textures (street, brick,
car paint). Hooks swap in real art: `art` (2D standee), `skin` (PNG),
`SOUND_FILES` (recordings).

See docs/adr/0011-procedural-art-in-code.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: A cutaway, not transparency, for buildings in the way
description:
The row between the camera and the street sinks to ground-floor ruins
(scaled to 14% height), and rises when the camera turns away.

See docs/adr/0010-building-cutaway.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Levels are data: map, theme and waves
description:
A level is `{ map, theme, waves }` in `src/data/config.ts`. The sim,
terrain, camera, minimap and world builder all take the active level. The
level comes from `?level=` (id or number); the title screen links to each.
Restarting reloads the page, keeping the level.

See docs/adr/0008-levels-as-data.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Ravines are rectangles to the rules, carved shapes to the eye
description:
To the rules a ravine is a rectangle of blocked nav cells. The visible
hole is a rounded, wobbly crack carved into the terrain that always stays
inside that rectangle (a test checks this). Flyers and giants follow the
ground surface as if ravines weren't there.

See docs/adr/0009-ravines-visual-inside-blocked-rect.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Speed up the whole game, not just zombies
description:
Add `GAME_SPEED = 2` and run the whole simulation faster (zombies,
plants, sun, cooldowns). The speed button multiplies on top.

See docs/adr/0007-whole-game-speed.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: ZomWes wanders when the base it attacks loses 25%
description:
Interpret it as the base being attacked: each time it loses another
quarter of its health, ZomWes moves to the base it visited longest ago.
Make it a config switch (`wanderOn: 'base' | 'self'`).

See docs/adr/0006-boss-wanders-on-base-health.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: The editor saves skins to the browser; defaults are committed PNGs
description:
Save to game stores the skin in `localStorage` (shared by the game and
`/editor/` because they're on the same site). The official skins are PNGs in
`public/skins/`; ⬇ PNG exports a skin to commit as the new default. A
saved skin whose size doesn't match the model's skin page is ignored.

See docs/adr/0005-editor-saves-to-browser.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Blocky part models with Minecraft-layout skins
description:
Characters are boxes (parts) with skins in the Minecraft skin layout,
at 128×128 by default. Models can attach parts to parts, taper parts, and
use bigger skin pages (the Westbot uses 256×256). Many zombies of one
type share a template mesh via instances.

See docs/adr/0004-blocky-models-minecraft-skins.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Pathfinding: nav grid + flow field, plants cost "chew time"
description:
A hidden 0.5-unit nav grid; one multi-source Dijkstra flow field to
the nearest standing base, rebuilt when plants or bases change. Plants are
passable at a cost equal to the time to chew through them, so zombies
detour when that's cheaper and chew when it isn't. Diagonal moves can't cut
past plant or obstacle corners. Giants and flyers skip the field.

See docs/adr/0003-flow-field-with-chewable-plants.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: A 2D fixed-step simulation, separate from rendering
description:
All rules live in `src/sim/`: a 2D simulation (x, z) on a fixed 30 Hz
step, seeded randomness, and an event list the renderer and audio consume.
Rendering (`src/render/`) only reads state and events. Height (hills,
ravines, leaps, flying) is visual only.

See docs/adr/0002-simulation-separate-from-rendering.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: ADR: Babylon.js, TypeScript and Vite, in the browser
description:
Use Babylon.js with TypeScript, built with Vite, deployed to
GitHub Pages. Babylon was chosen over Three.js because it brings the game
pieces we needed (cameras, glow layer, picking, particles, materials) without
assembling them ourselves. The HUD is plain HTML over the canvas.

See docs/adr/0001-babylonjs-browser-3d.md. Recorded retroactively.

title: Play-test spectacle on a real tablet
description: Cinematic timings, the dust-storm haze strength and particle counts (rain 4000, dust 1500) were only checked under software rendering at ~12 fps. Check feel and frame rate on the tablet; tune ROLL_IN, fog 0.034, emit rates and the boss shot if needed.

title: Index lookups and spatial hash in sim
description: Escorts call zombies.find(id) every tick; nearestZombie scans all zombies per plant. Keep Map<id, Zombie/Plant> and a uniform spatial hash (nav cells work) for big waves. Measure with a stress playthrough first.

title: Split main.ts; explicit UI mode state
description: main.ts (446 lines) holds input wiring, debug panel, loop and UI state. Extract input/controller.ts (taps/keys -> commands), debug.ts, session.ts. Replace the ui flag bag (selectedCard, aiming, selectedPlant, started…) with a mode union ('idle'|'placing'|'aiming'|'selected') so impossible combos can't happen (see the debug jump-to-wave handler resetting 5 fields).

title: Disposable game sessions (no reload on restart)
description: Restart reloads the page, so scene/game/HUD are never torn down. Add createSession(level, seed) -> { dispose() }. Enables level-to-level progression and retry without reload, and surfaces leaks that reloads hide (matters on tablets).

title: Theme builder registries; split decor.ts
description: world.ts checks theme.decor === 'ruinedCity', theme.rocks === 'carWreck', groundStyle === 'cityStreet' inline. Replace with DECOR, ROCK_STYLES, GROUND_STYLES, WEATHER registries (Record<Id, (ctx) => Disposable>). Split src/render/decor.ts (828 lines) per theme. A third theme adds entries only.

title: Versioned save envelope
description: Before saving progress/settings (skins already in localStorage), use { version, data } with migration functions so updates never corrupt saved progress. Build on serializable state.
